tagline: Eight suites, two jacuzzis and 5 or 6-day routes for 16 guests.
answer: New Galapagos Sea Star is a 42-metre Royal Galapagos yacht, refurbished in 2019. She carries 16 guests in 8 suites (4 Balcony Suites, 3 Galapagos Suites and the Sea Star Suite), with 10 crew, a cruise director and one bilingual naturalist guide. She sails 5 and 6-day routes linking San Cristobal and Baltra. Royal Galapagos calls her family-friendly, with interconnected and triple options.

overview: New Galapagos Sea Star is a 42-metre yacht refurbished in 2019, which Royal Galapagos describes as its newest luxury private yacht. Royal Galapagos is an Ecuadorian company running small yachts in the islands since 2012.

She takes 16 guests in eight suites. Four Balcony Suites on the Main Deck and three Galapagos Suites on the Upper Deck are each 25 square metres, and the Sea Star Suite on the Upper Deck is 35 square metres. All have private bathrooms, hot water and air conditioning; Royal Galapagos lists triple accommodation and interconnected cabins. On board there is a lounge, a reading corner, a bar, al fresco dining and a sundeck with two jacuzzis, plus internet.

Route A (6 days) runs from San Cristobal to Baltra via Espanola, Floreana, Santa Fe, South Plaza and North Seymour. Route B (5 days) loops from Baltra to Genovesa, Bartolome and Santiago. Route C (6 days) runs from Baltra to San Cristobal via southern and western Isabela, Fernandina and Santiago.
why: Suites for everyone: every cabin is a suite of at least 25 square metres, and the sundeck has two jacuzzis for 16 guests.
Royal Galapagos says she can reach both central and remote islands, and the three routes chain into 11 days or more.

children: Royal Galapagos does not publish a minimum age for this yacht. It gives children under 15 a 20% discount when one child shares a cabin with one full-paying adult (not with 2X1 promotions). Royal Galapagos calls Sea Star family-friendly, with triple accommodation and interconnected cabins.
